summary: Georg Morgenstierne worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Oslo, Bonn, and Humboldt University of Berlin (PhD 1914–1918) under Sten Konow, Heinrich Lüders, Hermann Jacobi, Hermann Beckh, and Wilhelm Schulze. He held professorships at Gothenburg (1930–1937) and Oslo (1937–1962).

Linguist Georg Renatus Solta earned his PhD at the University of Vienna (1934–1939), where he studied under Paul Kretschmer and Wilhelm Havers. He spent his career at the University of Vienna, becoming Privatdozent in 1953 and extraordinary professor of Indo-European linguistics in 1967.
Georg Simmel was a philosopher who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1876 to 1881. He later held an academic post there from circa 1885 to 1914.

Philosopher Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel studied at the University of Tübingen, Tübinger Stift, and University of Jena, studying under F. W. J. Schelling. He held positions at Jena, Aegidianum Nürnberg, Heidelberg University (circa 1816–1818), and Humboldt/Frederick William University Berlin (1818–1831).

Georg von Simson is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Mainz and Göttingen (PhD 1957–1965) under Ernst Waldschmidt. He worked at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities and was a professor at the University of Oslo from 1977 to 2003.

Georg von der Gabelentz worked in Sinology, linguistics, and Japanology. He studied at Jena, Halle-Wittenberg, TU Dresden, and Leipzig (PhD circa 1875–1876) under Hans Conon von der Gabelentz and August Friedrich Pott. He held professorships at Leipzig (1878–1889) and Berlin (1889).

Sinologist and linguist George A. Kennedy studied at Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1932 to 1935 under Erich Haenisch and Otto Franke. He subsequently held a post at Yale University from circa 1935 to 1960.

George A. Keyworth is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at UC Santa Barbara and UCLA (PhD 2001) under Ronald Egan, William F. Powell, Shuizhao Wang, and Robert E. Buswell Jr. He held posts at UC Boulder (2001) and Saskatchewan (2011).

George Abraham Grierson was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Trinity College Dublin under Robert Atkinson, Cambridge, and Halle-Wittenberg (PhD 1894). He served in the Indian Civil Service, was Superintendent of the Linguistic Survey of India (1898–1928), and directed SOAS (1917–1925).

Indologist George Adolphus Jacob was educated at Sheffield Collegiate School. He served as a colonel in the Indian Army and Bombay Staff Corps (circa 1857–1895), was acting superintendent at Poona's Native Army School (1862–1865), and became a fellow of the University of Mumbai.

Indologist George Baumann earned his PhD at Heidelberg University by 1973 and studied at the Bibliothekar-Lehrinstitut des Landes Nordrhein-Westfalen (circa 1973–1975). He worked at the University of Tübingen and as a Bibliotheksreferendar at Tübingen University Library from 1976 to 2001.

George Bidie worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Edinburgh and Marischal College, Aberdeen (MD circa 1849–1853). His posts included professor of botany at Madras Medical College (1866–1870) and superintendent of the Government Museum, Chennai (1872–1884).
George Bogle was a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed his education at Enfield Academy and the University of Edinburgh.

George Bosworth Burch worked in philosophy and Indology. He studied at Harvard (AB circa 1919–1923), Geneva, and Paris. He taught as a professor of philosophy at the College of Idaho (1942–1946) and Tufts University (1946–1967), and held visiting professorships in India.
George Byres Mainwaring was an Indologist and linguist. He served as an ensign in the Bengal Army in 1842 and as a lieutenant-colonel in the Bengal Staff Corps in 1868.

Indologist George C. O. Haas earned his AB and PhD (circa 1903–1909) under A. V. Williams Jackson at Columbia University. He taught German at City College of New York (1904–1916) and served as editor for the Journal of the American Oriental Society (circa 1916–1920).

George Campbell was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He completed his studies at Edinburgh Academy, Hamilton Academy, Madras College, the University of St Andrews (circa 1838–1840), East India Company College (circa 1841–1842), and the University of Oxford (DCL 1874).

George Cardona was an Indologist and linguist who studied at NYU and Yale under Warren Crawford Cowgill and Paul Thieme, alongside several traditional Indian teachers. He spent his academic career as a professor of linguistics at the University of Pennsylvania from circa 1965 to 2005.
George Carstairs worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied at The Albany Academy and attended the University of Glasgow, where he earned an MA (circa 1897–1901) and a DD (circa 1935).

George Chatalian was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned an AB at Brown University and a PhD at Harvard University in 1968. He held teaching posts at Franklin Pierce University, Obafemi Awolowo University (1983), and the University of Lagos.
